margins & cost dynamics:
The margin bridge management gave, in their own terms:
- **Sourcing mix:** domestic APM + NWG ≈ **40%**; long-term contracts ≈ **48%**; balance spot. By origin: **domestic ~62%**, **imported RLNG ~38%** (Brent-linked + Henry-Hub-linked).
- **Spot ≈ 15% of total consumption after the curtailment** — this is the bleeding wound.
- **Two cost shocks stacked:** (i) imported RLNG cost up on the West Asia crisis; (ii) **NWG price = 12% of the Indian crude basket**, so Brent >**$107/bbl** dragged the *domestic* leg up too — *"not only the imported RLNG costs have gone up but... the NWG prices also went up, which has impacted overall the gas cost."* NWG ran **>$5/MMBTU**.
- **APM allocation "going slowly down"** — the structural, non-cyclical part of the compression, admitted plainly by the CEO.
- **Mitigation:** move spot exposure into **mid-term** purchases now (*"not on the short term because the prices are elevated for the shorter term"*) and **long-term** contracts once the market stabilises; contracts coming up for renewal.
- **Pricing lever deliberately under-used:** on CNG, *"If you see the arbitrage between petrol and CNG, there is a room, but at the same time, we have to be conscious of fact of bringing more customers on board"* — volume prioritised over margin, again.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **No rupee capex figure disclosed** — only "slightly higher budget compared to last year," monitored "end-to-end" against the gas scenario. That is a softer commitment than it sounds.
- A **dedicated task force** has been created for domestic PNG connections.
- New models being explored to accelerate connections: **reticulated systems** and converting existing **LPG reticulated infrastructure** to PNG after safety diligence.
- **Slippage watch:** Q4FY26 cadence guidance was ~1 CNG station/week (~13/quarter) and ~400 home connections/day (~36,000/qtr). Q1FY27 delivered **5 stations** (≈40% of cadence) and 38,000 households (on cadence). **Station roll-out is the slip.**
capital allocation: Nothing disclosed — no net debt, no dividend, no returns commentary this call. ESG ratings improved (**CareEdge 84/100, CRISIL 66/100**), positioned as best-in-peer-group.
risks & watch-items:
1. **Pooled-gas withdrawal is the single biggest swing factor.** Removed *after* the peace deal — mgmt called it *"the sudden decision by the government."* Restoration is a hope, not a plan: *"probably some positive news should come shortly on that part **if the Middle East tension is not getting over**"* — i.e. ATGL now needs the crisis to *persist* for the subsidy mechanism to return, an uncomfortable dependency.
2. **Spot at ~15% of volume at peak prices** — direct, un-hedged P&L exposure with no stated timeline to close.
3. **APM allocation structurally declining** — permanent margin headwind, not cyclical.
4. **No margin recovery date.** *"if you ask me to predict... it would be very difficult."*
5. **FY27 EBITDA guide (₹1,500cr) silently unaddressed** — Q1 run-rate implies ~₹1,124cr. Either a miss is coming or a back-loaded recovery must be articulated next quarter.
6. **CNG station build-out slowed sharply** (+5 vs +25) while CNG demand grows ~30% — either capex discipline or execution slippage; mgmt was not asked.
7. **Skilled-manpower shortage** in PNG (gas plumbing/fitting) — mitigated industry-wide via ITI/diploma tie-ups and a new government skill course, but flagged as a real onboarding constraint.
8. **Competition in overlapping CGD areas** acknowledged — pricing set GA-by-GA "on almost everyday basis."
management quality / tone: Sober and noticeably less promotional than Q4FY26 — a **new CEO (Sanjay Pandita)** running his first call, with the sourcing head (Ravindra Desai) doing the analytical heavy lifting and being genuinely transparent on mix, spot % and the NWG formula. But the call was **short (8 pages, ~6 analysts)** and management **withheld PAT, PBT, net debt, capex quantum, EBITDA/scm and all EV economics**, and did not volunteer that the prior FY27 EBITDA guide is off-track. Declining to fabricate a margin-recovery date is honest; not reconciling to the prior guide is not.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The pooled-gas mechanism was withdrawn *because* of peace, not war.** ATGL is now structurally rooting for either full normalisation (cheap LNG) or continued tension (pool restored) — the worst outcome is exactly where it sits: post-deal, pre-supply.
- **NWG is Brent-linked at 12% of the Indian crude basket** — most models treat "domestic gas" as a price shock-absorber; here 62% domestic mix gave far less protection than it appears.
- **Revenue +27% vs volume +13%** ⇒ realisation up ~12% YoY. ATGL *is* passing through, just not fast enough — the gap is roughly the ₹5/SCM cost move.
- **Government now expects fertiliser gas demand to fall post-sowing**, which mgmt believes frees domestic volume for CGD — the quiet, monsoon-seasonal upside nobody models.
- **I&C customer adds at 3x/2x YoY** is the most under-discussed positive on the call; nobody asked what it does to volume mix.
- EV: 3.3mn electrons at 5,306 CP works out to ~620 electrons/CP for the quarter — utilisation is still the unanswered question mgmt itself named as the focus.

margins & cost dynamics:
The margin bridge management gave, in their own terms:
- **Sourcing mix:** domestic APM + NWG ≈ **40%**; long-term contracts ≈ **48%**; balance spot. By origin: **domestic ~62%**, **imported RLNG ~38%** (Brent-linked + Henry-Hub-linked).
- **Spot ≈ 15% of total consumption after the curtailment** — this is the bleeding wound.
- **Two cost shocks stacked:** (i) imported RLNG cost up on the West Asia crisis; (ii) **NWG price = 12% of the Indian crude basket**, so Brent >**$107/bbl** dragged the *domestic* leg up too — *"not only the imported RLNG costs have gone up but... the NWG prices also went up, which has impacted overall the gas cost."* NWG ran **>$5/MMBTU**.
- **APM allocation "going slowly down"** — the structural, non-cyclical part of the compression, admitted plainly by the CEO.
- **Mitigation:** move spot exposure into **mid-term** purchases now (*"not on the short term because the prices are elevated for the shorter term"*) and **long-term** contracts once the market stabilises; contracts coming up for renewal.
- **Pricing lever deliberately under-used:** on CNG, *"If you see the arbitrage between petrol and CNG, there is a room, but at the same time, we have to be conscious of fact of bringing more customers on board"* — volume prioritised over margin, again.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **No rupee capex figure disclosed** — only "slightly higher budget compared to last year," monitored "end-to-end" against the gas scenario. That is a softer commitment than it sounds.
- A **dedicated task force** has been created for domestic PNG connections.
- New models being explored to accelerate connections: **reticulated systems** and converting existing **LPG reticulated infrastructure** to PNG after safety diligence.
- **Slippage watch:** Q4FY26 cadence guidance was ~1 CNG station/week (~13/quarter) and ~400 home connections/day (~36,000/qtr). Q1FY27 delivered **5 stations** (≈40% of cadence) and 38,000 households (on cadence). **Station roll-out is the slip.**
capital allocation: Nothing disclosed — no net debt, no dividend, no returns commentary this call. ESG ratings improved (**CareEdge 84/100, CRISIL 66/100**), positioned as best-in-peer-group.
risks & watch-items:
1. **Pooled-gas withdrawal is the single biggest swing factor.** Removed *after* the peace deal — mgmt called it *"the sudden decision by the government."* Restoration is a hope, not a plan: *"probably some positive news should come shortly on that part **if the Middle East tension is not getting over**"* — i.e. ATGL now needs the crisis to *persist* for the subsidy mechanism to return, an uncomfortable dependency.
2. **Spot at ~15% of volume at peak prices** — direct, un-hedged P&L exposure with no stated timeline to close.
3. **APM allocation structurally declining** — permanent margin headwind, not cyclical.
4. **No margin recovery date.** *"if you ask me to predict... it would be very difficult."*
5. **FY27 EBITDA guide (₹1,500cr) silently unaddressed** — Q1 run-rate implies ~₹1,124cr. Either a miss is coming or a back-loaded recovery must be articulated next quarter.
6. **CNG station build-out slowed sharply** (+5 vs +25) while CNG demand grows ~30% — either capex discipline or execution slippage; mgmt was not asked.
7. **Skilled-manpower shortage** in PNG (gas plumbing/fitting) — mitigated industry-wide via ITI/diploma tie-ups and a new government skill course, but flagged as a real onboarding constraint.
8. **Competition in overlapping CGD areas** acknowledged — pricing set GA-by-GA "on almost everyday basis."
management quality / tone: Sober and noticeably less promotional than Q4FY26 — a **new CEO (Sanjay Pandita)** running his first call, with the sourcing head (Ravindra Desai) doing the analytical heavy lifting and being genuinely transparent on mix, spot % and the NWG formula. But the call was **short (8 pages, ~6 analysts)** and management **withheld PAT, PBT, net debt, capex quantum, EBITDA/scm and all EV economics**, and did not volunteer that the prior FY27 EBITDA guide is off-track. Declining to fabricate a margin-recovery date is honest; not reconciling to the prior guide is not.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The pooled-gas mechanism was withdrawn *because* of peace, not war.** ATGL is now structurally rooting for either full normalisation (cheap LNG) or continued tension (pool restored) — the worst outcome is exactly where it sits: post-deal, pre-supply.
- **NWG is Brent-linked at 12% of the Indian crude basket** — most models treat "domestic gas" as a price shock-absorber; here 62% domestic mix gave far less protection than it appears.
- **Revenue +27% vs volume +13%** ⇒ realisation up ~12% YoY. ATGL *is* passing through, just not fast enough — the gap is roughly the ₹5/SCM cost move.
- **Government now expects fertiliser gas demand to fall post-sowing**, which mgmt believes frees domestic volume for CGD — the quiet, monsoon-seasonal upside nobody models.
- **I&C customer adds at 3x/2x YoY** is the most under-discussed positive on the call; nobody asked what it does to volume mix.
- EV: 3.3mn electrons at 5,306 CP works out to ~620 electrons/CP for the quarter — utilisation is still the unanswered question mgmt itself named as the focus.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth:** No number given. Asked directly for revenue guidance, CEO deflected to volume: *"if you see our volume growth, that will continue to grow in a similar manner"* → read as **~13% volume growth continuing**. **Last quarter's explicit ~18% revenue / ₹1,500cr EBITDA FY27 guide was NOT reaffirmed and was not mentioned once.**
- **Margin:** **No timeline.** *"once this crisis in Middle East is over... we'll see the margins improving to the last level or better than that"* — event-contingent, not date-contingent. On being pressed for a 9–12-month scenario, mgmt would only cite mid-term and long-term gas purchases as the lever.
- **PNG connections:** *"We would at least maintain the same rate at which we are right now doing it"* → **≥38,000 households/quarter**.
- **EV charge points:** **10,000 CP target** reaffirmed — *"This strong momentum reinforce our confidence in achieving our targets of 10,000 EV charging points"* (no date attached; 5,306 today).
- **Capex:** *"we have slightly higher budget compared to last year"* — **no rupee number**, and explicitly conditioned on monitoring the gas scenario.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Government's long-term ambition to raise natural gas's share in India's primary energy mix to 15% by 2030 (from ~6-6.5% currently) continues to guide CGD ecosystem expansion
- India's natural gas demand expected to grow at 8-9% CAGR through 2030, driven by CGD expansion, fertiliser demand and increasing adoption of gas as a transport fuel
- New Geographical Areas are maturing faster than the base: volumes in new GAs grew 32% YoY, with the newer-GA volume mix improving to 38% from 32% in FY25, underscoring growing acceptance of the expanding network
- CNG continues to outpace PNG growth: CNG volumes rose 18% YoY versus ~6% for PNG, on continued network expansion and customer-focused initiatives
- Policy tailwinds expected to accelerate adoption: simplified natural gas pipeline transportation tariffs for home PNG/CNG, CST applicability on interstate gas movement, and state-level CGD policy adoption/VAT rationalisation
- Diversified gas sourcing strategy is management's primary lever to offset gas cost pressure (up ~23% YoY) while maintaining supply continuity across customer segments
- Early-stage investments in e-mobility and compressed biogas are expected to mature as these segments are poised to grow amid the push to reduce reliance on imported energy sources
- A threefold surge in home PNG connection enquiries followed the geopolitical (West Asia) situation, handled via proactive outreach and digital infrastructure

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
The margin bridge management gave, in their own terms:
- **Sourcing mix:** domestic APM + NWG ≈ **40%**; long-term contracts ≈ **48%**; balance spot. By origin: **domestic ~62%**, **imported RLNG ~38%** (Brent-linked + Henry-Hub-linked).
- **Spot ≈ 15% of total consumption after the curtailment** — this is the bleeding wound.
- **Two cost shocks stacked:** (i) imported RLNG cost up on the West Asia crisis; (ii) **NWG price = 12% of the Indian crude basket**, so Brent >**$107/bbl** dragged the *domestic* leg up too — *"not only the imported RLNG costs have gone up but... the NWG prices also went up, which has impacted overall the gas cost."* NWG ran **>$5/MMBTU**.
- **APM allocation "going slowly down"** — the structural, non-cyclical part of the compression, admitted plainly by the CEO.
- **Mitigation:** move spot exposure into **mid-term** purchases now (*"not on the short term because the prices are elevated for the shorter term"*) and **long-term** contracts once the market stabilises; contracts coming up for renewal.
- **Pricing lever deliberately under-used:** on CNG, *"If you see the arbitrage between petrol and CNG, there is a room, but at the same time, we have to be conscious of fact of bringing more customers on board"* — volume prioritised over margin, again.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, ATGL commissioned 9 new City Gas Stations (CGS) and 1 new LCNG facility in newer Geographical Areas recently connected to the national gas grid, taking total operating CGS to 26 and LCNG to 5. Steel pipeline network expanded to 15,572 inch-km and MDPE pipeline to 8,306 km, with domestic PNG connections crossing 10.99 lakh households (1.37 lakh new connections added) and CNG stations reaching 705, including expansion of CODO/DODO models to 140 stations. Through wholly owned subsidiary Adani TotalEnergies E-Mobility Limited (ATEL), the EV charging network grew to 5,100 installed charge points (4,265 energised) across 225+ cities and 22 airports, adding 26 MW of charging capacity during the year to reach 54 MW installed; ATEL's near-term plan is to scale to around 10,000 charge points across key urban and mobility corridors via a calibrated, asset-light BOHO (Build-Operate-Handover) model. Through wholly owned subsidiary Adani TotalEnergies Biomass Limited (ATBL), Phase 1 of the agri-waste-to-CBG plant at Barsana, Uttar Pradesh was commissioned with 10 TPD production capacity (peak production of 7.5 TPD achieved in FY26), expected to ramp up to 11 TPD in FY 2026-27; pre-development work began on municipal solid waste-based CBG projects in Ahmedabad and Rajkot, and the 'Harit Amrit' brand was launched in MP, UP and Gujarat. Joint venture IndianOil-Adani Gas Private Limited (IOAGPL) tied up new debt facilities of approximately Rs 3,100 crore to fund its planned capital expenditure programme and completed a CCD transaction of Rs 1,400 crore, positioning it to accelerate CGD network build-out across new Geographical Areas. Joint venture Smart Meters Technologies Private Limited (SMTPL) operates a gas-meter manufacturing facility at Gangad, near Ahmedabad, with an annual production capacity of approximately 7.2 lakh meters.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Sober and noticeably less promotional than Q4FY26 — a **new CEO (Sanjay Pandita)** running his first call, with the sourcing head (Ravindra Desai) doing the analytical heavy lifting and being genuinely transparent on mix, spot % and the NWG formula. But the call was **short (8 pages, ~6 analysts)** and management **withheld PAT, PBT, net debt, capex quantum, EBITDA/scm and all EV economics**, and did not volunteer that the prior FY27 EBITDA guide is off-track. Declining to fabricate a margin-recovery date is honest; not reconciling to the prior guide is not.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **Pooled-gas withdrawal is the single biggest swing factor.** Removed *after* the peace deal — mgmt called it *"the sudden decision by the government."* Restoration is a hope, not a plan: *"probably some positive news should come shortly on that part **if the Middle East tension is not getting over**"* — i.e. ATGL now needs the crisis to *persist* for the subsidy mechanism to return, an uncomfortable dependency.
2. **Spot at ~15% of volume at peak prices** — direct, un-hedged P&L exposure with no stated timeline to close.
3. **APM allocation structurally declining** — permanent margin headwind, not cyclical.
4. **No margin recovery date.** *"if you ask me to predict... it would be very difficult."*
5. **FY27 EBITDA guide (₹1,500cr) silently unaddressed** — Q1 run-rate implies ~₹1,124cr. Either a miss is coming or a back-loaded recovery must be articulated next quarter.
6. **CNG station build-out slowed sharply** (+5 vs +25) while CNG demand grows ~30% — either capex discipline or execution slippage; mgmt was not asked.
7. **Skilled-manpower shortage** in PNG (gas plumbing/fitting) — mitigated industry-wide via ITI/diploma tie-ups and a new government skill course, but flagged as a real onboarding constraint.
8. **Competition in overlapping CGD areas** acknowledged — pricing set GA-by-GA "on almost everyday basis."

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The pooled-gas mechanism was withdrawn *because* of peace, not war.** ATGL is now structurally rooting for either full normalisation (cheap LNG) or continued tension (pool restored) — the worst outcome is exactly where it sits: post-deal, pre-supply.
- **NWG is Brent-linked at 12% of the Indian crude basket** — most models treat "domestic gas" as a price shock-absorber; here 62% domestic mix gave far less protection than it appears.
- **Revenue +27% vs volume +13%** ⇒ realisation up ~12% YoY. ATGL *is* passing through, just not fast enough — the gap is roughly the ₹5/SCM cost move.
- **Government now expects fertiliser gas demand to fall post-sowing**, which mgmt believes frees domestic volume for CGD — the quiet, monsoon-seasonal upside nobody models.
- **I&C customer adds at 3x/2x YoY** is the most under-discussed positive on the call; nobody asked what it does to volume mix.
- EV: 3.3mn electrons at 5,306 CP works out to ~620 electrons/CP for the quarter — utilisation is still the unanswered question mgmt itself named as the focus.
